title: Cannabis for Stress May Disrupt the Stress System
hook: Frequent cannabis users woke up with cortisol already elevated — raising the possibility that using it to relax gradually dysregulates the system that handles stress.
key_points: Frequent users showed unusually high morning levels of the stress hormone cortisol.
Cortisol normally follows a daily rhythm, peaking shortly after waking.
An altered pattern suggests the stress-response system is dysregulated.
Many people use cannabis specifically to relieve stress.
The finding raises the question of whether that use undermines stress handling over time.
content_html: Plenty of people use cannabis to take the edge off. A study of frequent users found something that complicates that story: their stress hormone was already running high before the day began.
extra_html:
As ScienceDaily reports, frequent cannabis users woke with unusually elevated levels of cortisol. Cortisol normally follows a clear daily rhythm — rising sharply in the first minutes after waking, then tapering through the day — and a distorted version of that curve is a standard signal that the stress-response system isn't regulating itself well.

The researchers' framing is a question rather than a verdict: if people reach for cannabis precisely because it relieves stress, does frequent use gradually interfere with the machinery that handles stress on its own? This study can't establish direction — people under more chronic stress may simply use cannabis more — but it does undercut the assumption that the calming effect is free. It also rhymes with what's known about alcohol used the same way, where the short-term relief and the long-term effect on stress regulation point in opposite directions.

related.title: What Stress Does to Your Body
related.hook: A jolt of stress is useful — it sharpens you for a real threat. The problem is when the alarm never switches off, and the body pays for staying on high alert.

related.title: Drinking to Cope With Stress May Permanently Rewire the Brain
related.hook: Using alcohol to cope with stress at a young age may permanently change the brain — making it harder to adapt to future challenges and raising the risk of drinking again later in life.

related.title: Teen Cannabis Use and the Slowing of Thinking Skills
related.hook: Teens who started using cannabis kept developing normally at first — then their memory, attention, and processing speed leveled off while non-users kept improving.

flashcards.prompt: What did researchers observe in frequent cannabis users' cortisol?
flashcards.back_html: They woke up with unusually high levels of cortisol, the stress hormone — suggesting their daily stress rhythm is disrupted rather than calmed.

flashcards.prompt: Why is this finding awkward for using cannabis as a stress reliever?

choices.text: The short-term relief may come at the cost of dysregulating the stress system itself
It shows cannabis has no effect on mood at all
It proves cortisol has nothing to do with stress

flashcards.explanation_html: Many people use cannabis specifically to unwind. If frequent use leaves the body's cortisol rhythm disrupted, the immediate calm may be undermining the very system that handles stress over the longer run.
